text:
Marie: Heads up — after onboarding ranker-v3-int4 we see inconsistent NDCG/MRR on long-context queries when a leading whitespace priming token is used. Quick repro in the eval harness attached.
Kevin: can you paste the repro snippet and confirm this is offline harness vs prod?
Marie: offline harness. quick config: ```python
# eval config snippet
seqlen = 1024
tokenizer = 'hf/roberta-fast'
pad = 'right'
priming = ' '  # single leading space as priming
batch_size = 64
quant = 'int4'
```
Anya: Hmm padding direction + tokenizer differences often cause off-by-one subtoken shifts. Are you using the same tokenizer binaries as runtime?
Marie: Not exactly — harness uses tokenizers v0.13 python backend; runtime uses our fast C++ wrapper (same vocab but different pretoken logic). Suspect subword boundary changes with leading space.
Devon: Could quantization be amplifying small score ties? If candidates swap when scores are close, that could blow up NDCG. Did you try a deterministic seed + disable kv cache fallback?
Marie: ran seed=42 and kvcache=false. Delta persists but fewer flips.
Olga: Also check chunk/truncation policy. For long docs, adding one priming token shifts the cutoff window which can change which sentence is included — that can change relevance more than you'd expect.
Kevin: +1. Confirm the offline eval chunks by token count while prod chunks by sentence boundaries for that dataset? That mismatch would explain asymmetric behavior.
Marie: Plan: 1) re-run offline eval using the runtime tokenizer (hf fast) 2) test pad='left' and pad='right' 3) run without priming to get baseline 4) compare fp16 vs int4 to measure quant gap. Who can pick up step 1?
Anya: I can run 1 and 2 on a 10k query slice and post the diffs. ETA ~2h.
Devon: As a quick mitigation, we could canonicalize candidate text before tokenization: strip leading whitespace and normalize internal spaces. That should reduce boundary-induced churn.
Marie: Agreed — add canonicalizer to eval harness only for now and see if signal stabilizes. I'll also add an eval flag to emit token offsets so we can inspect boundaries. Example sample row: ```json
{'query_id': 'Q12', 'doc_id': 'D123', 'tokens': ['ĠThe','re','st'], 'offsets': [0,4,7] }
```
Olga: FYI I plotted a per-query token-delta histogram; there's a clear spike at +1 token for the primed long-doc cohort. Link: https://redwood.internal/plots/priming-token-delta :bar_chart:
Marie: thanks — tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-ml for visibility in case we want runtime changes (tokenizer canonicalization) vs eval-only fixes.
Kevin: If Anya's runs show it goes away with runtime tokenizer, we should 1) standardize tokenizers between harness and runtime 2) add a unit test that compares token boundaries for a small set of golden docs.
Anya: pushed first run results, small sample shows NDCG drop reduces from 3.8% to 0.7% when using runtime tokenizer. Posting CSV.
Devon: Ok that points to tokenization mismatch. Let's prioritize harmonizing tokenizers for bring-up. Also create a quick CI check that flags >1% NDCG delta from tokenizer-only changes.
Marie: sounds good. I'll open a follow-up ticket and add action items. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
